answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A canyon delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A ember check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A willow penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 2971 identities need 2971 bonds of 75 tokens, 44803 dollars of hardware and 54 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
